pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are all 0 and that 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' only when starred; test 'AC-2' checks exact list output.
WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and checks the order.
Test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all return all items in id order.

The code has the links, and a test checks them. But the last commit (4b87571 'Follow-up edits') renamed that test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other', so no test names AC-5. Under the review rules an item no test names and the spec doesn't mark is unmet.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400 for other values; test 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__, and checks there is no <li>.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; test 'AC-7' asserts it. Traffic's check() builds the URL from the path, so the query is kept.

findings.what: The final commit 'Follow-up edits' removed the 'AC-5:' prefix from the link test's title. As a result no test names AC-5, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. The PR body says tests cover AC-1 to AC-7, which is no longer true. The commit message hides what the commit does.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'. Name the 'Starred only' and 'All items' link checks explicitly.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the last commit changed a test title, which loosened the traceability. The commit is also named 'Follow-up edits', which doesn't describe it.
findings.fix: Revert the rename, or mention it in the PR body.

lenses.note: The spec is present. The decisions are followed: the order is kept (ORDER BY id with no starred sorting) and the view is a GET query parameter.
All four state-table rows have tests. AC-5 is not named by any test (see finding).
The tests assert exact rendered output and would fail on broken code. I did not run them: they need the Workers runtime and CI covers them. The AC-5 naming gap is a finding.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The traffic-config check's route regex now allows a query string, and its tests cover that.
The Object.hasOwn guard blocks __proto__ values. The SQL is built only from fixed VIEWS entries, not from user input. The migration is additive.
The show value is validated against a fixed allow-list. Titles are escaped. The new route regex still refuses spaces and '#'. No planted instructions found.
The change is a trivial server-rendered HTML link and list; no UI style or component files in the diff.
No browser or UI flow to demonstrate in this review; the states are covered by tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is slightly off because of the final test rename.
